source_signature.notes: Batch 4J skill 4/5. Owns the CONVENTION itself rather than any computation: the assume-tension convention for structural members (every unknown member force assumed positive in tension, a negative solved value meaning compression); the physical meaning that a member in tension pulls both of its end joints toward each other while a member in compression pushes both of them apart; the fact that the ARROW on a joint free-body diagram REVERSES between a member's two ends while the member's SIGNED VALUE does not change; CROSS-METHOD CONSISTENCY, so the same member reads the same signed value whether reached by joints or by section; and reporting a signed result with a T or C designation rather than a bare magnitude. Boundary: method_of_joints (signed, skill 2) and method_of_sections (signed, skill 3) both USE this convention and both name this skill as its owner; the artifact carries the complement - those skills compute member forces, this one owns the convention they apply, member values are taken as GIVEN, and 'do not recompute' is authored into both the procedure and the prompt rather than left implicit. internal_force_sign_convention (signed, Batch 4H) is the direct beams-family analogue - it owns the N/V/M convention, the equal-and-opposite relationship between the two faces of a cut, and signed rather than bare-magnitude reporting - and this skill is its truss-member counterpart. truss_support_reactions (signed, skill 1) supplies reactions, given not re-derived. zero_force_members (batch sibling, position 5) is excluded with a stated reason: a zero-force member has no sign to assign. Worked example Operator-verified against the same truss analysed by method_of_sections: joints A(0,0) pin, D(4,0), E(8,0), G(12,0) on the bottom chord and B(4,3), F(8,3) on the top; nine members; loads 6 kN down at D and 24 kN down at E; reactions Ax = 0, Ay = 12 kN up, Gy = 18 kN up. Member values given from both signed methods: F_BF = -16, F_DF = -10, F_DE = +24 by method of joints propagating A then B then D, and identically by method of sections cutting BF, DF and DE. Interpretation under the convention: F_BF = -16 kN is 16 kN COMPRESSION, F_DF = -10 kN is 10 kN COMPRESSION, F_DE = +24 kN is 24 kN TENSION. Distinguishing feature bites: compression and tension are both present so the sign carries meaning; ARROW REVERSAL is demonstrated explicitly for one member of each state - for BF the unit direction from B toward F is (1,0) giving a force on B of (-16,0) pushing B AWAY from F, while the unit direction from F toward B is (-1,0) giving a force on F of (+16,0) pushing F AWAY from B, opposite arrows with the signed value -16 at both ends; for DE the force on D is (+24,0) pulling D TOWARD E and the force on E is (-24,0) pulling E TOWARD D, again opposite arrows with the signed value +24 at both ends and both arrows pulling the joints together; cross-method agreement is shown on all three members; and a magnitude-only report is detectably incomplete because 16 kN alone does not distinguish BF, which is in compression, from a tension member of the same magnitude. Reporting a member as positive at one end and negative at the other is the specific misconception this skill exists to correct, and the artifact names it directly. HONEST LIMITATION recorded in concept, procedure, solution and common_errors, and it is the subtlest in this batch: cross-method agreement confirms the VALUE but not the INTERPRETATION, because both methods rest on the same assumed-tension convention - if that convention were declared backwards both methods would agree and both would be wrong. The mapping from a negative value to compression is a declaration that must be stated, not something the agreement verifies. VERIFICATION PRECEDES REPORT in both arrays, and the verification is the cross-method comparison with that circularity caveat recorded alongside it. TWO-signal mapping, matching the shape of the beams analogue internal_force_sign_convention: sign_or_placement_error at step 3 (CENTRAL - reading the arrow direction at one end as the member's sign, reporting the member as positive at one end and negative at the other, or inverting the negative-to-compression mapping; its trigger opens by stipulating the given signed values are in hand, which partitions it from the interpretation inputs), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - magnitude-only report, omitted convention declaration, skipped cross-method check, recomputation by either method, or assigning a sign to a zero-force member). axis_confusion OMITTED with an explicit argument: this is a convention skill and no authored step resolves a force into components along a chosen axis; unit directions appear only to demonstrate arrow sense, which is not a resolution. The beams analogue omitted it for exactly the same reason, and the two-signal shape was reached by argument rather than by targeting a count. solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: no authored step strands a prerequisite unknown. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family). Trig-resolution cross-check N/A recorded affirmatively: no inclined vector is decomposed from a stated angle. No archetype is asserted while PROCEDURE-ARCHETYPE-LIBRARY-V1 remains unapproved. Review beat cleared at first pass; no correction lane.
